top_choice_rationale: P001 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is the most mature and best-attributed discovery on the slate: the magic-wavelength lattice concept is simple and checkable, 10^-18 performance has been reproduced and compared between independent laboratories, and the clocks now yield new measured quantities (millimetre-scale redshift, limits on drifting constants). It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control citations, though the Sr-lattice priority history still deserves expert verification. P002 (aberration-corrected TEM) is a genuine invention that I use in my own field, but it is an enabling instrument and the uncredited STEM corrector work of Krivanek, Dellby and Lupini makes the three-name attribution contestable. A prize is still better than none, so P000 is last.
